target_customer: People sending mass messages to user-defined groups across text, email and instant messaging
problem: Group messages reach people on only one channel; recipients may be on SMS, email or IM.
business_model: Not found; messaging platform with focus on mass mobile messaging to groups

founders.name: Julia West
founders.background_notes: Only founder named on the YC page; no background found

competitors.name: Meebo
competitors.what: Browser based multi-protocol instant messaging with no download; adjacent to Jumpchat's no-download IM bridge
competitors.traction_then: Matched eBuddy's traffic within four months per Fortune

competitors.name: eBuddy (formerly E-Messenger)
competitors.traction_then: Had web chat market largely to itself before Meebo per press

technical_complexity.rationale: Bridging SMS gateways, email and IM protocols into one conversation required carrier integration and message routing in 2006.

defensibility.rationale: Carrier SMS gateways were available to anyone and no unique asset or network is described.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source says what incumbents did to Jumpchat.

market_need_then: Mobile texting and web IM both grew in 2006, but no source found shows demand for Jumpchat itself.

branding.domain_note: jumpchat.com now hosts an unrelated video chat product per AlternativeTo; the fetch of the site returned empty.

brand_strength.rationale: No press or brand material found; later products reuse the name.

pivots.from: Bridge across mobile text, email and IM
pivots.to: Mass mobile messaging to user-defined groups
pivots.why: YC page says the current focus is mass mobile messaging; no date or reason given

outcome_analysis: Jumpchat bridged text messages, email and instant messaging for group sends and narrowed to mass mobile messaging, per the YC page. It is listed Inactive. A 2012 TNW article says it did not work out without giving a reason, and no funding, shutdown date or post mortem was found, so the cause of failure is not public in the sources checked.
notes: Funding: nothing found; Dealroom team page paywalled. Loot-drop.io describes a 2006 to 2009 run and a video chat product with no cited source; treated as unreliable and not used. Meebo and eBuddy are adjacent web IM players, not direct matches; Meebo article dated two months after batch start. YC page location listed as San Francisco in the data and Palo Alto in a search snippet. Cause of inactivity not public.
